title: Vasopressors or Fluids in Early Septic Shock
shortTitle: ARISE FLUIDS: early vasopressors did not improve hospital-free survival
authors: ARISE FLUIDS Investigators, the ANZICS Clinical Trials Group, and the ACEM Clinical Trials Network
summary: This trial randomized 1,000 adults presenting to EDs with septic shock to restricted fluids with earlier vasopressors or more fluids with later vasopressors. Among 963 patients in the intention-to-treat population, median days alive and out of hospital at day 90 were 76 in both groups.
whyItMatters: A universal vasopressor-first strategy did not improve the primary outcome. Fluid tolerance and perfusion response should continue to inform resuscitation rather than assuming one strategy fits every patient.
limitations: Thirty-seven randomized patients lacked consent for inclusion. Different fluid and vasopressor exposure did not establish equivalence or identify the optimal strategy for individual patients.
population: Adults presenting to emergency departments with septic shock.
intervention: Restricted fluid volumes and early vasopressor therapy for 6-24 hours.
comparator: Higher fluid volumes and later vasopressor therapy.
primaryEndpoint: Days alive and out of hospital through day 90.
findings: Vasopressor strategy reduced first-day fluid by a median 1,108 mL.
Pulmonary edema: 0.6% with the vasopressor strategy versus 5.0% with the fluids strategy.
evidenceNotes: Abstract reviewed; full text unavailable. Complete indexed PubMed abstract reviewed and date cross-checked with publisher. Direct full-text request returned 403; no unauthorized copy used. October 8 print issue is not first-online date.
